tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomolo.summary: Mathlib supplies the canonical carrier and compatible-pair functoriality (continuousCohomology, homogeneousCochains, cochainsMap/cocyclesMap/map with map_id and map_comp, and ContinuousCohomology.zeroIso), and Tau Ceti has already built almost the whole low-degree half of the roadmap: the coefficient theory and continuous sections of Layer 0, the smooth-discrete dictionary and named res/infl/coeffMap of Layer 1, the complete explicit complex with its functoriality and conjugation homotopies (Layer 2), the discrete comparison in all three degrees (Layer 3), the finite-quotient system with the degree-0 and degree-1 colimits (Layer 4), the long exact sequence through degree 2 with its naturality (Layer 5), corestriction in degrees 0-2 with change-of-transversal and cor∘res (Layer 6), the coinduced module with exactness plus Shapiro in degrees 0 and 1 (Layer 7), all six cup shapes with associativity, graded commutativity, restriction, inflation and the projection formula (Layer 8), and the Kummer sequence, cocycle and class map (Layer 9). What is genuinely missing is the canonical-model half and the multiplicative theory: the degree-1 and degree-2 comparison with continuousCohomology, the degree-2 colimit universality and all coefficient-colimit statements, the transgression and five-term sequence, transitivity and Mackey for corestriction, Shapiro in degree 2 with its naturality and the coinduction adjunction, the connecting-map cup identities and the Bockstein, profinite Hilbert 90 and hence the Kummer isomorphism and the whole galois* field-extension bridge. Layers 10 to 13 are essentially unbuilt: there is no all-degree long exact sequence, corestriction, Shapiro, dimension shifting or torsion statement, no cohomological dimension of a profinite group at all, no all-degree graded cup product, and no Evens norm — though Tau Ceti's TauCeti.WreathProduct already supplies the permutation wreath product that Layer 13's first milestone asks Mathlib's regular version to be generalized to.

targets.target: Point stabilizers of a discrete module are open; continuity of the action is equivalent to openness of stabilizers
targets.note: Cited by the roadmap itself as a Mathlib prerequisite and used verbatim in TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Discrete.lean:52.

targets.target: For finite M the kernel of the action is open, so the action factors through a finite quotient
targets.note: `openActionKernel` is an `OpenNormalSubgroup G` acting trivially on a finite discrete M over profinite G; `finite_quotient_toPermHom_ker` gives the finite quotient. Hypotheses are [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] [Finite M]. No sorry in the file.

targets.target: For arbitrary discrete M over profinite G, every element is fixed by an open normal subgroup and M = ⋃_U M^U
targets.note: `iSup_fixedPoints_openNormal_eq_top` is exactly the union statement Layer 4 consumes; the finite-set refinement is proved first.

targets.target: Invariants M^U as a G ⧸ U-module for normal U, with the induced discrete action
targets.note: The file deliberately reuses Mathlib's `MulAction.fixedPoints` and the quotient action on the fixed points of a normal subgroup rather than a parallel `Invariants`; the added content is continuity of the G ⧸ U-action, proved for OpenNormalSubgroup and for any normal H with continuous action.

targets.target: Finite products of discrete modules, and subgroups and quotients with induced/quotient topologies, are again discrete G-modules
targets.note: These are instance-level closure facts rather than named theorems: `Pi.discreteTopology` carries [Finite ι], the subtype instance is Mathlib/Topology/Constructions.lean:200, and TauCeti supplies discreteness of a quotient by a submodule. The roadmap explicitly excludes infinite products and direct sums.

targets.target: For finite M and discrete N the internal hom M →+ N with conjugation action (g•φ)m = g•φ(g⁻¹•m) is a discrete G-module
targets.note: `homAction` is the stated conjugation formula; openness of the stabilizers (hence discreteness of the action) is `isOpen_setOfPred_homAction_eq_self`, and the open-normal-subgroup form is proved for finite M. File has no sorry.

targets.target: Evaluation pairing (M →+ N) →+ M →+ N is G-equivariant
targets.note: Exactly the pairing Layer 8's duality package and the Class Field Theory roadmap are said to consume.

targets.target: Continuous section of G ⧸ K → G ⧸ H for closed K ≤ H ≤ G, and the normalized G ⧸ H → G with s 1 = 1 (Ribes–Zalesskii 2.2.2)
targets.note: Hypotheses are [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] and IsClosed (H : Set G); the conclusion includes the normalization s (mk 1) = 1 exactly as the roadmap asks. The right-coset factorization is the extra shape Layer 7 consumes. No sorry.

targets.target: Extension lemma: a continuous map from a closed subspace of a profinite space into a finite discrete target extends continuously
targets.note: Proved for any discrete (not just finite) nonempty target over a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected X, which is more general than the stated target; the range-control clause is the form that keeps the extension inside a subgroup. No sorry.

targets.target: The carrier TopRep R G and Hⁿ_cont(G,X) = continuousCohomology n X, with homogeneousCochains and the degree-0 iso
targets.note: Mathlib's `ContinuousCohomology.zeroIso` is the roadmap's `continuousCohomologyZeroIso`; `TopRep` is a definition of its own in Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Continuous/TopRep.lean with an equivalence to Action (TopModuleCat R) G rather than an abbreviation for it. No sorry in these files.

targets.target: IsSmoothDiscrete, and its closure under restriction along a continuous homomorphism
targets.note: The predicate and the named counterexample (a discrete object that is not smooth) are both present, which is the roadmap's stated reason for the subcategory.

targets.target: Closure of the smooth discrete objects under finite products, subobjects and quotients
targets.note: Only closure under restriction is proved. The file's own Roadmap section (SmoothDiscrete.lean:85-90) records that product/subobject/quotient closure 'is not yet statable, because Mathlib's TopRep carries no limit, subobject or quotient API to state it against'. The unbundled Layer-0 analogue is available from Mathlib instances, but the bundled statement is missing.

targets.note: `discreteRepEquivSmoothTopRep` is the mutually-inverse equivalence between DiscreteRep R G and SmoothDiscreteTopRep R G; `ofDiscreteModuleHomAddEquiv` is the statement that every morphism between objects in the image arises from an equivariant map. Stated for an arbitrary topological ring R and a monoid G wherever possible, i.e. more generally than ℤ.
